target: Recover collection after a same-size rollout metadata rewrite and allow the macOS user transaction to finish its readiness and rollback window.
primary_semantics: Persist a full-file SHA-256 for complete rollout cursors, verify later same-size metadata changes against it, and keep the outer updater alive longer than the complete inner transaction.
invariants: Raw conversations, summaries, indexes, configuration, and the active archive root remain unchanged by installation.
A persisted source byte hash mismatch fails closed.
Legacy complete cursors may acquire a baseline byte hash only while their committed byte count still equals the source size.
Routine macOS updates remain user-space transactions with rollback.
allowed_changes: Add an optional source byte hash to Codex cursor metadata, align the outer update timeout, update release metadata, and add focused regression coverage.
prohibited_changes: Rewrite rollout files, raw archive records, summaries, or indexes.
Remove rollback, invoke the system Installer for routine updates, or add installation-time downloads.
before_after_checks: A same-size mtime-only change seeds or verifies the source byte hash and collection reaches ready.
A same-size content change fails when a prior source byte hash exists.
The macOS updater timeout exceeds the collector readiness timeout plus post-switch checks.
Version, documentation, architecture, and platform tests remain consistent.

original_triggers: A same-size rollout rewrite could bypass size-only source identity checks.
The outer updater timeout could expire before the inner readiness and rollback transaction completed.
